analytic.title: An Automatic Configuration Approach to Improve Real-Time Application Throughput While Attaining Determinism

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Determinism and throughput are two important performance measures for Java-based real-time applications, but they often conflict. Therefore, it is significant to improve throughput for Java-based real-time applications while guaranteeing its execution time determinism. In this paper, we propose an automatic configuration approach to assign realtime thread priorities to solve the above-mentioned problem. In this approach, we propose an innovative representation of determinism related with real-time thread priorities using stochastic process. Java-based real-time application's throughput is quantified with thread priorities as parameters. The algorithm of integer programming is used to optimize throughput with boundary conditions of the level of determinism. Finally, the Sweet Factory application is tested to evaluate the effect of our approach. Experiment results show that throughput for Java-based real-time applications could be efficiently improved while keeping the execution time determinism with our approach.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Java-based real-time applications have received increasing attention from real-time software development communities with the support of Java real-time virtual machine technologies. These technologies, including realtime garbage collector and ahead-of-time class loading and compilation, increase the execution predictability of Java code. As a consequence, Java real-time applications can not only meet the real-time requirements, but also inherit the advantages of Java language, such as high abstraction level and portability.

Unlike traditional Java application, the primary performance criterion for Java-based real-time application is not the average execution time, but determinism. That means response time should be guaranteed predicable. Determinism can be measured as the variation of response time or execution time, which generally raises more concern than execution speed for some real-time applications. And it can be ensured by Java real-time virtual machine through realtime garbage collector, real-time scheduler, etc. These technologies, however, have negative impacts on the application's execution speed. As we know, throughput has positive correlation with the execution speed. Consequently, determinism is ensured at the expense of decreasing throughput for these applications.

Therefore, it is important to increase throughput while guaranteeing the determinism for Java-based real-time applications. The main challenges to make trade-off between throughput and determinism are as follows:

• Identify the application features that are related with determinism and throughput; • Measure determinism and throughput through either analytical or numerical approach. The goal of this paper is to achieve a better tradeoff between determinism and throughput through an automatic approach. First, we analyze the real-time application features and model real-time threads with these features. And then we propose an innovative approach to represent determinism with application features using stochastic process, and develop a formula to express throughput with these features. Then we optimize throughput under the constraint of determinism using integer programming algorithm. Finally, we evaluate our approach with a specific application Sweet Factory [1]. The experiment results verify the effect and the efficiency of our approach. This paper's major contribution can be outlined as:

• Abstract the application features related to determinism and throughput and integrate these features into the representation of determinism and throughput with stochastic process in a mathematical way; • Propose a flexible approach to automatically configure the application features in order to guarantee its determinism and optimize its throughput. To reflect our goal, the rest of this paper is structured as follows: Section II introduces our motivating example scenario. Section III describes our innovative approach to improve the real-time application throughput. Section IV evaluates the effect of our approach. Section V discusses related works and makes a comparison with our work. Section VI concludes and discusses the future work.

div.head: II. MOTIVATION
div.p: To better illustrate our work of improving real-time application's throughput, we first introduce a motivating example that will be revisited several times through the course of this paper. Sweet Factory example represents a classical scenario inspired by [1]. Its task is to design an automation system controlling an output statistics from a production line in a sweet factory and report all anomalies. There is a production line that periodically generates measurements about the sweet jars. Then a monitoring system evaluates these jars whether they are over or under filled. A worker console is notified whenever abnormal measurements appear. Also there is an auditing log which records all the measurements into a log file. The production line should operate in predetermined intervals; the application therefore should meet real-time requirements.

As is shown in Fig. 1, real-time and non-real-time concerns are blended together, and they interact with each other. Based on our analysis, determinism of the application is not only closely related to the configuration of real-time thread priorities, but also the dependency of these threads. Additionally, the application's throughput is also linked to these factors. So it is not easy to model the relationship among real-time thread priorities, dependency, determinism and throughput. As a consequence, the developers and deployers of real-time applications have to face the issue of assigning real-time thread priorities properly in order to optimize the throughput and guarantee the determinism.

Solving the above issue during the development and deployment phase is therefore an inconvenient process. To avoid this, an approach of automatically configuring the realtime thread priorities is urgently required. Moreover, the way of representing determinism and throughput should be not only with high ability of expression, but also concise.

div.head: III. APPROACH FOR AUTOMATICALLY CONFIGURING REAL-TIME THREAD PRIORITIES
div.p: Determinism of real-time threads is affected by several factors, such as their priorities, their dependency on other threads and timing requirements. In this paper, we propose an automatic configuration approach to clarify the relationship between determinism and these factors, and describe it using stochastic process. Additionally, we express throughput using the above-mentioned factors in a mathematical way based on our qualitative analysis. In our approach, we discuss determinism from the thread perspective, and talk about throughput at the level of the whole application.
Fig. 2 illustrates the overview of the approach, which is composed by the following parts:

div.head: A. Model of Real-Time Threads
div.p: Priority is crucial to determinism of the real-time thread. The higher the priority, the better the determinism is achieved. Moreover, thread dependency also has an impact on determinism. In other words, if a real-time thread A counts on the results of another thread B, then A's determinism is relevant to B's properties. In addition, timing requirement is fundamental to a real-time thread, which is as important as its functional features. Therefore, our model of real-time threads describes a real-time thread with three factors: i.e., thread priority, dependency and required response time. div.head: B. Representation of Determinism
div.p: In our approach, determinism is measured as the variation of response time. The less the variation, the higher the determinism is achieved. Real-time thread priority and determinism show a positive correlation characteristic. The higher the priority, the greater the determinism is. The priorities of threads in its dependency set also have an impact on its determinism, and they have shown positive correlation.

div.head: C. Representation of Throughput
div.p: Throughput denotes the speed at which the real-time application runs. Therefore in our approach, throughput is measured as the inverse of application's execution time. In order to guarantee determinism, the average execution time of an application is prolonged. Thus throughput is influenced by the effort of ensuring determinism. The higher priorities real-time threads have, the harder the thread scheduling optimization can be achieved. Hence, throughput has a negative correlation with real-time thread priorities.

Besides the real-time thread priorities, thread dependency also exerts an influence on throughput. However, the relationship between throughput and thread dependency is complicated and is not easy to quantify. Thus we try to clarify the relationship from the execution flow perspective and analyze the impact of threads with high priorities on the whole application's throughput. Fig. 4 illustrates an execution flow chart. We call the relationship between Thread 2 and Thread 3 sibling, as shown in Fig. 4. Through our qualitative analysis, we notice that the relative relationship among sibling threads' priorities affects the whole application's throughput. For example, if Thread 2 has higher priority than Thread 3, then more computing resource is allocated to Thread 2 and the execution time of Thread 3 is lengthened. As Thread 6 depends on Thread 3, the whole application's execution time is under the influence Hence, we model the thread dependency relationship from the sibling perspective to quantify the application's throughput. div.head: D. Automatic Configuration Algorithm
div.p: In order to obtain an improved thread priority assignment, we need to find a proper algorithm to solve the problem of maximizing the whole application's throughput while guaranteeing its level of determinism, as abstracted in Fig. 5. There have been many reusable algorithms [5] to deal with multi-dimensional optimization problems. In our approach, we adopt Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) model [6,7] to generate the thread priority configuration. Until now, there are several MINLP solvers available from research institutions. And we choose the solver Baron (Branch-And-Reduce Optimization Navigator) [8,9] developed by University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign to compute the thread priority assignment. Baron is a computational system for solving non-convex optimization problems to global optimality. It can deal with the problems efficiently, such as purely continuous nonlinear programs, purely integer and mixed-integer non-linear programs. Therefore, this solver could meet our demand well.

To represent our problem for MINLP, we should first define the decision variable P i , which indicates the priority assigned to thread i τ . Then solver Baron tries to find the assignment for each P i to make Throughput maximized.

div.head: IV. EVALUATION
div.p: In this section, we evaluate the effect and efficiency of our approach, which automatically assigns real-time thread priorities with the purpose of improving throughput and attaining determinism. Our experiments are based on the hardware platform of Lenovo Qitian M6900 with Intel Pentium Process E5400 and RAM of 1G DDRII 800, and the software platform of Solaris 10 Update 9 [10] and Sun Java Real-Time System 2.2 [11]. Our experiment platform is aimed at providing upstanding real-time environment for Java applications. Solaris' real-time capability is based upon its initial kernel design which is capable of bounded dispatch latency for real-time threads. And Sun Java Real-Time System (RTS) is Sun's implementation of Real-Time Specification for Java (RTSJ) [4] including a real-time garbage collector which allows real-time applications to avoid unpredictable delays commonly caused by traditional garbage collectors.

div.head: C. The Effect of Our Configuration on Real-Time Thread
div.p: Response Time While obtaining the experiment results that illustrate the effect of our framework on the whole application's throughput, we also need to conduct experiments to verify whether our configuration can still guarantee the determinism of response time.

We take the thread TriageRunnable as an example, record its response time, and make the comparison. These experiments are derived from the execution of Sweet Factory application composed by three production lines. And we keep a continuous record of TriageRunnable's response time to each event under the original and our improved thread priority configurations. Fig. 7 shows the response time results under different configurations. The evaluation shows that the determinism of response time is guaranteed under our improved configuration compared with the original one.

div.head: D. The Impact of Our Configuration on the Consumption of CPU Resources
div.p: While we have demonstrated the effect of our configuration on throughput and illustrated that our configuration has no significant impact on determinism, we also need to compare the consumption of CPU resources under the original and our improved thread priority configurations. And we compare their consumption of CPU resources under different number of production lines. Fig. 8 demonstrates the average CPU utilization rate under different priority configurations. Each point in Fig. 8 indicates the average CPU utilization rate consumed by the application consisted of a certain number of production lines. In order to guarantee the accuracy of the data, we conduct five independent experiments under each case. Then these results are averaged as the data shown in Fig. 8. The experiment results illustrate that our improved configuration occupies 4.5% more CPU resources than the original configuration averagely. Under the case of three production lines, our configuration consumes about 5.7% more CPU resources. As shown in Fig. 8, with the increase of the number of production lines, the amount of consumed CPU resources, that our configuration exceeds the original one, declines.

The above evaluation shows that our automatic configuration approach could generate a real-time thread priority configuration, which could increase the application's throughput by 20% averagely. Moreover, our improved configuration has no significant impact on the determinism of response time. Though our configuration consumes relatively more CPU resources, the benefit that we obtain from the configuration, i.e., the improvement of throughput, is still much greater than the cost we pay.

div.head: V. RELATED WORKS
div.p: There are currently several research works on quantitative analysis of real-time embedded applications [12,13,14,15].

Wandeler et al. [12] have introduced an approach to compute analytical upper and lower bounds on performance measures of real-time applications, such as throughput and resource utilization. The calculation model can be derived from the system specification and the model of the system environment. And it allows the comparison of design alternatives according to parameter changes. Compared to their work, our approach mainly focuses on the relationship between throughput and determinism and exploits the tradeoff between them. Gutierrez et al. [13] have proposed an optimized priority assignment heuristic, which iteratively computes deadlines for individual tasks and messages in the system based on the deadline-monotonic policy. Their algorithm is efficient both in quality and especially in speed. Their approach is mainly concerned with how to assign thread priority to meet their corresponding deadline well. Compared with their work, our approach tries to generate a thread priority configuration which could not only improve the application's throughput but also ensure its determinism.

Lobry et al. [14] have proposed a set of flexibilityoriented properties to be selectively applied to the architectural elements in a given architecture. These properties are used to optimize the code. This framework makes the development of embedded application more flexible in order to meet the requirement of increasing complexity and restrained physical resources. Compared to their work, we are also trying to solve a tradeoff issue, but we mainly focus on adjusting the application properties from the execution thread perspective, instead of the architectural perspective.

Phan et al. [15] have proposed a model in the form of automata to analyze timing properties for embedded systems, which processes complex event and data streams and copes with mode changes triggered by both time and event. The model pieces together the analytical results from different modes into the performance metrics for the whole system. Compared with their work, our approach adopts stochastic process to describe the behavior of actual response time with real-time application properties.

div.head: VI. CONCLUSION
div.p: This paper proposes an automatic configuration approach to generate real-time thread priority assignment with the purpose of improving real-time application's throughput while guaranteeing its determinism. We adopt stochastic process to represent real-time application's determinism and quantify the relationship between determinism and throughput in the form of mathematical model. We transform the problem of improving throughput while assuring its determinism into an integer programming problem and adopt MINLP solver Baron to solve this critical issue. The example and experiment results show that our approach significantly improves real-time application's throughput. And our realtime thread priority assignment has no significant impact on its determinism.

There are still several issues to be addressed in the near future. One is how to extend our single factor model, i.e., only considering real-time thread priorities, to a multiple factor model taking other factors into account, such as the type of memory used by the thread and so forth. Another is how to improve the application's throughput from both the virtual machine and the application perspective, i.e., how to adjust both the parameters of virtual machine and the properties of real-time application in order to improve the whole application's throughput while attaining its determinism.

div.head: B. The Effect of Our Configuration on Throughput
div.p: Based on the configuration obtained from Section IV.A, we conduct the following experiments to illustrate the effect of our approach on improving throughput. Sweet Factory is an automation system with several production lines that transform raw ingredients into different sorts of sweets and then put them into jars. The greater the throughput, the larger the number of jars produced by the production lines is. In our experiments, we test the effect of our optimized configuration under different number of production lines. Fig. 6 demonstrates the experiment results. Each point in Fig. 6 indicates the total number of jars produced by the production lines within one minute. In order to guarantee the accuracy of the data, we conduct five independent experiments under each case. Then these results are averaged as the data shown in Fig. 6.
